title: The Kind Bird
description: Read the story, then answer the questions in your own words.
story:
Last Saturday, Maya was playing in her backyard when she noticed a small bird on the ground. Its wing looked hurt, and it could not fly.

Maya carefully placed the bird in a small box with soft cloth. She then called her uncle, who was a veterinarian. Together, they took the bird to the animal clinic. The vet wrapped the bird's wing and said it would heal in two weeks.

Maya visited the bird every day, bringing seeds and water. After two weeks, the bird was strong again. Maya took the box outside, opened it, and watched the bird fly into the sky. She felt proud knowing she had saved a life.

title: The Lion and the Mouse
description: Read this classic fable, then answer the questions.
story:
One sunny day, a tiny mouse ran across a sleeping lion's paw. The lion woke up angrily and trapped the mouse with his huge claw. Please let me go! begged the mouse. One day I might help you in return. The lion laughed loudly. How could a tiny mouse ever help a king like him? But the lion let him go.

A few weeks later, hunters caught the lion in a strong rope net. The lion roared and roared, but he could not escape. The little mouse heard the roar and remembered the lion. The mouse ran to the net and chewed through the ropes with his sharp teeth. Soon the lion was free.

Thank you, my small friend, said the lion. I see now that even the smallest creatures can do great things.

title: Place Value, Standard & Expanded Form, Rounding
description: Read the Key Vocabulary box, then answer each question.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. PLACE VALUE
The value of where a digit sits in a number.
   495: 4=Hundreds(400), 9=Tens(90), 5=Ones(5)

2. STANDARD FORM
Writing a number using digits.
   two thousand forty = 2,040

3. EXPANDED FORM
Breaking a number to show each digit's value.
   356 = 300 + 50 + 6

4. ROUNDING
Make a number simpler by rounding to nearest ten or hundred.
   RULE: Look at the digit to the RIGHT of where you round.
   5 or more = round UP.  4 or less = round DOWN.
   79 rounds UP to 80.  34 rounds DOWN to 30.  462 rounds to 500.

title: Estimation, Unknown Numbers & Inverse Operations
description: Read the Key Vocabulary box, then answer each question.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. FRONT-END ESTIMATION
Keep the highest place value digit, make the rest zeros.
   458 → 400   678 → 700   311 → 300

2. UNKNOWN NUMBER
A missing number shown as ? or a letter.
   24 + ? = 83  →  83 - 24 = 59  →  ? = 59
   A - 42 = 200  →  200 + 42 = 242  →  A = 242

3. INVERSE OPERATIONS
The OPPOSITE operation that UNDOES another.
   Addition undoes Subtraction.  Multiplication undoes Division.

4. DECOMPOSE (Expanded Subtraction)
   678 - 548 = ?
   600+70+8 minus 500+40+8 = 100+30+0 = 130

title: Multiplication Properties
description: Read the Key Vocabulary box, then answer each question.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. COMMUTATIVE PROPERTY
Order does NOT matter when multiplying.
   3 x 4 = 12  AND  4 x 3 = 12 (same answer!)

2. ZERO PROPERTY
Any number x 0 = 0.
   5 x 0 = 0.  999 x 0 = 0.

3. IDENTITY PROPERTY
Any number x 1 = that number.
   225 x 1 = 225.  7 x 1 = 7.

4. DISTRIBUTIVE PROPERTY
Break one factor into a sum of two smaller facts.
   6 x 4 = (3 x 4) + (3 x 4) = 12 + 12 = 24

title: Division: Fact Families & Repeated Subtraction
description: Read the Key Vocabulary box, then answer each question.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. DIVISION
Separating a whole amount into EQUAL parts.
   20 / 4 = 5 means 20 split into 4 groups = 5 in each.

2. DIVIDEND / DIVISOR / QUOTIENT
   20 / 4 = 5
   20 = DIVIDEND (number being split)
   4  = DIVISOR (number of groups)
   5  = QUOTIENT (number in each group)

3. FACT FAMILY
All related x and / facts for the same 3 numbers.
   2 x 4 = 8 | 4 x 2 = 8 | 8 / 4 = 2 | 8 / 2 = 4

4. REPEATED SUBTRACTION
Subtract the same number over and over until you reach 0.
   12 / 3: 12-3=9, 9-3=6, 6-3=3, 3-3=0. Answer = 4.

title: 2D Shapes: Triangles, Quadrilaterals & Angles
description: Read the Key Vocabulary box, then answer each question.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. TRIANGLES
A 2-D closed shape with exactly 3 sides and 3 angles.
   Equilateral Triangle = ALL 3 sides are equal.

2. QUADRILATERAL
Any polygon with FOUR sides.
   Types: Square, Rectangle, Rhombus, Parallelogram, Trapezoid, Kite.

3. ANGLE & RIGHT ANGLE
   Angle = formed when two line segments meet at a vertex.
   Right Angle = exactly 90 degrees (looks like a square corner).

4. VERTEX (plural VERTICES)
   The corner where two or more sides meet.
   Triangle = 3 vertices.  Square = 4 vertices.

Lines that always stay the same distance apart and NEVER cross.

title: Fractions: Numerator, Denominator & Equivalents
description: Read the Key Vocabulary box, then answer each question.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. FRACTION
An amount broken into equal size pieces.
   Written as: numerator / denominator.  Example: 1/2

2. NUMERATOR
The TOP number. Tells HOW MANY parts we have.
   In 3/6, numerator = 3.

3. DENOMINATOR
The BOTTOM number. Tells the TOTAL equal parts in the whole.
   In 3/6, denominator = 6.

4. EQUIVALENT FRACTIONS
Different fractions that are equal in value.
   1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8
   Use > or < to compare fractions.

title: Measurement: Length & Time
description: Read the Key Vocabulary box, then answer each question.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. LENGTH UNITS
   Inches (in) — 12 inches = 1 foot
   Quarter inch = 1/4 of an inch
   Half inch = 1/2 of an inch
   Feet (ft) = 12 inches
   Yards (yd) = 3 feet (football field = 100 yards!)

2. PERIMETER
The distance AROUND a shape. Add all sides!
   Rectangle 15cm x 5cm: 15+5+15+5 = 40 cm

3. TIME
   Minute = 60 seconds
   Hour = 60 minutes
   1 day = 24 hours

4. ELAPSED TIME
How much time has passed between start and end.
   Start 3:30 PM, End 4:05 PM = 35 minutes elapsed.

title: Area, Perimeter & Square Units
description: Read the Key Vocabulary box, then answer each question.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. SQUARE UNIT
A square with an area of 1. Used to measure area.
   Written as cm2, in2, ft2, etc.

2. AREA
The SPACE INSIDE a shape.
   Area of Rectangle = Length x Width
   8 cm x 3 cm = 24 cm2

3. PERIMETER (Review)
Distance AROUND the outside.
   P = L+W+L+W or P = 2L + 2W
   8 cm x 3 cm rectangle: P = 8+3+8+3 = 22 cm

4. AREA MODEL
A rectangle drawn to show a multiplication problem.
   Used for distributive property too!
   6 x 4 split as (3x4)+(3x4) = 12+12 = 24

title: Data & Graphs
description: Read the Key Vocabulary box, then answer each question.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. TALLY MARKS & FREQUENCY TABLE
   Tally mark = a way to count (4 lines + 1 crossing = 5)
   Frequency table = organized table showing how often things occurred.

2. BAR GRAPH
Represents data with vertical or horizontal bars.
   X Axis = BOTTOM horizontal line of the graph.
   Y Axis = SIDE vertical line of the graph.

3. PICTURE GRAPH
Uses pictures/symbols to show data.
   Each symbol has a KEY showing how many it represents.
   Example: smiley face = 2 votes

4. READING DATA
   HOW MANY MORE = subtract the two values
   HOW MANY TOTAL = add all values
   Dogs=10, Cats=8, Snakes=5, Rabbits=2 → Total = 25

title: Surah An-Naba — Complete (All 40 Ayat)
description: Read ALL 40 ayat with your parent. Read Arabic, transliteration, and meaning. Then answer the questions!
story:
SURAH AN-NABA (The Great News) Surah 78
Read each ayah aloud with your parent!

── PART 1: THE QUESTION (Ayat 1-5) ──
1. Amma yatasaa-aloon — About what are they asking one another?
2. Anil naba-il azeem — About the great news
3. Allathee hum feehi mukhtalifoon — That over which they disagree
4. Kalla saya-lamoon — No! They are going to know.
5. Thumma kalla saya-lamoon — Then, no! They are going to know.

── PART 2: ALLAH'S SIGNS (Ayat 6-16) ──
6. Alam naj-alil arda mihadaa — Have We not made the earth a resting place?
7. Wal jibala awtadaa — And the mountains as stakes?
8. Wa khalaqnakum azwajaa — And We created you in pairs.
9. Wa ja-alna nawmakum subataa — And made your sleep a means of rest.
10. Wa ja-alnal layla libasaa — And made the night as clothing.
11. Wa ja-alnan nahara ma-ashaa — And made the day for livelihood.
12. Wa banayna fawqakum sab-an shidadaa — And built above you seven strong heavens.
13. Wa ja-alna sirajan wahajaa — And made a blazing lamp (the sun).
14. Wa anzalna minal mu-sirati ma-an thajjajaa — And sent down from the rain clouds pouring water.
15. Linukhrija bihi habban wa nabataa — That We may bring forth grain and vegetation.
16. Wa jannatin alfafaa — And gardens of entwined growth.

── PART 3: THE DAY OF JUDGMENT (Ayat 17-20) ──
17. Inna yawmal fasli kana meqataa — Indeed, the Day of Judgment is an appointed time.
18. Yawma yunfakhu fis suri fata-toona afwajaa — The Day the Horn is blown and you come in multitudes.
19. Wa futihatil sama-u fakanat abwabaa — And the heaven is opened and becomes gateways.
20. Wa suyyiratil jibalu fakanat sarabaa — And the mountains are removed and become a mirage.

── PART 4: THE PUNISHMENT (Ayat 21-30) ──
21. Inna jahannama kanat mirsadaa — Indeed, Hell has been lying in wait
22. Lil tagheena ma-abaa — For the transgressors, a place of return.
23. Labiteena feeha ahqabaa — In which they will remain for ages unending.
24. La yathooqoona feeha bardan wa la sharabaa — They will taste no coolness, nor any drink
25. Illa hameeman wa ghassaqaa — Except scalding water and foul purulence.
26. Jaza-an Wifaqaa — A fitting recompense.
   ★ MEMORIZE AYAH 26: Jaza-an (recompense) + Wifaqaa (fitting)
27. Innahum kaanu la yarjoona hisabaa — Indeed, they were not expecting an account.
28. Wa kaththabu bi-ayatina kiththabaa — And denied Our signs with emphatic denial.
29. Wa kulla shay-in ahsaynahu kitabaa — But all things We have enumerated in writing.
30. Fathooqoo falan nazeedakum illa ataabaa — So taste the penalty; We will increase only your torment.

── PART 5: REWARD FOR THE RIGHTEOUS (Ayat 31-36) ──
31. Inna lil muttaqeena mafazaa — Indeed, for the righteous is attainment
32. Hada-iqa wa a-naabaa — Gardens and grapevines.
33. Wa kawa-iba atrabaa — And companions of equal age.
34. Wa ka-san dihaqaa — And a full cup.
35. La yasma-oona feeha laghwan wa la kiththabaa — No ill speech or falsehood will they hear.
36. Jaza-am mir rabbika ataa-an hisabaa — A generous reward from your Lord.

── PART 6: THE FINAL TRUTH (Ayat 37-40) ──
37. Rabb is-samawati wal ardi wa ma baynahuma ar-rahmani la yamlikoona minhu khitabaa — Lord of the heavens and earth, the Most Merciful. None can speak without His permission.
38. Yawma yaqoomur roohu wal mala-ikatu saffan — The Day the Spirit and angels stand in rows. None speak except whom the Most Merciful permits.
39. Thalikal yawmul haqq — That is the True Day; whoever wills may return to his Lord.
40. Inna antharnakum ataaban qareeban yawma yanthorul mar-o ma qaddamat yadahu wa yaqoolul kafiru ya laytani kuntu turabaa — We warned you of a near punishment. On that Day a man sees what his hands have done, and the disbeliever says: I wish I were dust!
